summary: Three pins surface two problem families: a concrete operational gap (installed Rust binary drifting from source after cli.rs edits) and a strategic failure (V2 widget shipped a plugin contribution-point framework when three concrete tools were requested, compounding across multiple 'not useful' signals instead of pivoting on the first). The cargo/cli.rs issue is a concrete Rust instance of the named binary-rebuild mistake pattern. The V2 story is the highest-signal pin: it names a moment where an 'architecturally professional' choice diverged from the user's grounded need, and the agent repeatedly added surface rather than questioning the premise.

insights.instruction: Watch for this in future events: after any Edit targeting src/cli.rs, flag that the installed binary is now stale and cargo install must run before claiming the CLI change is live.

When a user says 'not useful' after a feature ship, do not add more surface. Stop and audit whether the architectural premise matches the user's actual grounded need. Concrete user requests are not prompts to generalize into a framework.

summary: Three pins from 2026-05-29 split across two problem surfaces: a catastrophic compound failure in the Versable frontend agent session exposing a performative-self-criticism anti-pattern and a hinter pipeline gap, and two structural bugs in i-dream itself where both the daily digest and the interactive audit generate fresh data instead of reading authoritative persisted state. The Versable pin is the most complex — it names five known live slugs that still failed to correct in-session behavior, suggesting enforcement surface (UserPromptSubmit) is insufficient. The i-dream pins share a root cause worth associating: consumers that silently discard persisted state in favor of re-generation.

A single high-signal pin describes a cross-cutting false-positive class in raw-command-string-scanning hooks: guards that match dangerous tokens anywhere in a shell invocation string will trip on documentation prose, RCA content, and here-doc bodies that discuss the very commands being blocked. The cli-gating subsystem already solved this (quoted-string awareness + 150 tests), but safe-delete and guard-system-dir-writes have not adopted the fix. The actionable dream output is a refactoring proposal and a shared helper extraction to unify all five scanning hooks under the same command-position-aware parser.

insights.instruction: Extract a shared `is_token_in_command_position(token, argv)` helper — reusing cli-gating's existing quoted-string and heredoc-body parsing logic — and thread it through safe-delete.sh, guard-system-dir-writes.sh, comment-hygiene, and env-access hooks. ci-gating's 150-test suite becomes the regression harness for all five.
When reviewing any new guard/hook proposal, apply the same context-awareness bar as for ADR exceptions: ask 'does this matcher understand the grammatical position of the token, or only its presence?'

Add a hook-authoring checklist item to PLACEMENT.md or scripts/hooks/README.md: 'Does this hook scan raw command strings? If yes, does it use the shared command-position parser? If no shared parser exists yet, implement one in lib/ and adopt it here.'

summary: Two pins from 2026-06-19 capture the graduation arc of the ai-smell-prose-against-stored-voice S3 atone event (mist-20260619-194539-c9) into rules/audience-aware-writing.md, which is now live in CLAUDE.md Tier-0. The graduation rule side is complete; the mechanical enforcement side — Stop-stage prose hook prop-20260619-194931-ba — remains status:open. Historical precedent from source-comment-hygiene (same class of advisory rule, same account) and the Versable hinter-failure session (pin-20260529152121-e6) both point toward the same conclusion: the advisory rule alone will not correct the pattern under pressure.

A single pin from 2026-06-21 grounds itself in a concrete ARG_MAX bug caught by immediately exercising a new vision command against real data the instant the model finished downloading. The latent theme is not the bug itself but its cause: the user's 'reliability over performance' evaluation axis drove the immediate exercise and surfaced what static inspection would have missed. This preference refines and unifies three existing patterns — exercise-based-verification, structure-over-one-shotting, efficacy-over-speed — into an explicit trust hierarchy that should graduate into global memory.

insights.instruction: When any local-models bin/ tool processes image files or large text blobs, test it with a real-sized input before declaring done. Shell arg limits are silent — no warning, just truncation or ENOMEM. Pattern to watch: jq --arg combined with binary-to-base64 output or large model responses.
Audit bin/probe and any new bin/ commands added to local-models for the large-buffer-through-shell-args pattern. If found, apply the Python-inline or stdin-pipe pattern used in bin/see:82-103.

summary: The two new pins form a paired case study in the same failure class. The first (pin-20260624080929-6d) documents a 3rd S3 recurrence of speculative-abstractions despite a live rule, atone hints, and previous corrections, plus a double-recording slip from misreading background CLI silence as process death. The second (pin-20260624205747-54) shows the structural inverse: a design → adversarial-skeptic → cheap empirical test loop killing the same class of over-build before any code was written, with the three relevant atone slugs used as a predictive checklist rather than an after-the-fact guardrail. Together they reveal that slugs are diagnostic at design time but not corrective mid-session, and that an empirical test is what converts skeptic opinion into falsifiable fact.

The pinned insight captures a multi-rung integration ladder for using local-models as a decoupled Claude worker fleet. Cross-referencing docs/03 and docs/07 reveals the architectural decision is already resolved: deterministic pipeline (Claude conducts, q workers execute scoped single calls, Judge gate verifies) is canonical — model-driven loops are unanimously rejected by MAGI. The pin's open question about direct-calls vs Claude-called vs mix is a false dichotomy; the real invariant is whether the local model self-directs (rejected) vs executes a predetermined scope (approved).

insights.instruction: Before implementing any rung of the integration ladder, verify each q worker call has a PREDETERMINED SCOPE defined by the orchestrator (Claude), not by the local model. If the local model decides what file to read next or what tool to call next, it is the rejected MODEL-DRIVEN LOOP pattern.

When implementing docs/07 Phase-1, ensure the weekly self-audit emits events compatible with the atone JSONL schema (id, slug, severity, issue, fix fields) so i-dream can ingest fleet quality signals alongside session-level corrections without a schema adapter.

When routing a task, apply the split explicitly: HIGH-VOLUME + LOW-STAKES-PER-CALL + VERIFIABLE (review, recon, mechanical transforms) goes to local worker fleet; hard reasoning, design, synthesis stays with cloud sub-agents where peak intelligence justifies cost and throttle risk.

summary: The new pin describes a deferred architectural decision: generalize the claude-instances dashboard from a hard-coded Claude provider to an agentic-runner × model session dashboard. The pin already completed the options assessment (cheapest = separate lm/q calls panel; cleanest = provider interface abstraction) and explicitly defers the build choice to the weekly audit. This is a rare 'the thinking is done, the gate is a calendar event' shape — the useful dream work is surfacing the cross-association with pin-20260702191100-51 (worker-fleet integration) and flagging the concrete design invariant the cleanest option must not violate.

insights.instruction: The worker-fleet pin resolved orchestration architecture (Claude conducts, q workers execute predetermined scope). The dashboard pin is the observability layer for the same ecosystem. When building option (2)'s provider interface, the 'enumerate procs by pattern; parse tail → {model,state,activity}' contract maps directly to the fleet's worker-call JSONL schema — both surfaces read the same signal (model id, state, activity). Design them to share a parser rather than duplicating the transcript-tail logic. Cross-reference docs/07-implementation.md for the JSONL field names before authoring the provider interface.

insights.name: provider-coupling-in-observability-tooling
insights.instruction: scan.sh:492-521 hard-codes three provider assumptions: (1) binary name is exactly 'claude', (2) transcript dir is ~/.claude/projects, (3) a session == one transcript file. Before adding local-models or codex support, extract these three assumptions into a ProviderDef struct {proc_pattern, transcript_dir, session_glob, tail_parser} with the Claude implementation as the reference. Any new runner is then a new ProviderDef entry, not a new code path. If a runner's transcript format is incompatible with the tail_parser contract, implement a thin adapter — never branch on provider name inside the core scan loop.

insights.rationale: This pin is the second instance of a pin that says 'options assessed, decision deferred to weekly audit.' The pattern suggests the weekly audit needs an explicit agenda item: 'pins with deferred build decisions.' Without a calendar-backed queue, deferred decisions decay without resolution. Consider adding a recurring 'resolve deferred pins' step to the weekly audit ritual.

insights.name: option-1-cheapest-path-viable-now
insights.instruction: Option (1) — an lm/q calls panel reading ~/Code/local-models JSONL histories — is buildable today without any provider interface refactor because one-shot calls are not live sessions (separate panel, no proc enumeration needed). If the weekly audit decision leans toward proving value before committing to the cleanest option, implement option (1) as a standalone panel first. Verify ~/Code/local-models JSONL history path and field names before authoring the panel (cross-reference docs/07-implementation.md:1-50 per pin-20260702191100-51).

summary: Three pins from 2026-07-10/11 surface a shared epistemological pattern: in each session, a proposed build turned out to be unnecessary or wrong once the underlying platform/data was actually measured or audited. The IPC investigation killed an elegant architecture pre-build by measuring its key premise against a real corpus; the imagine CLI session found 28 existing backend tools rendering the gap purely a wiring problem; the ghostty V3 fork was retired the same day because the compositor already covered it. Two graduation candidates emerge: a standing extension-points-over-forks preference and a concrete imagine subcommand wiring proposal.

insights.instruction: When a proposed design depends on a behavioral ratio (fraction of X that are Y, hit rate, fraction answerable), collect a real sample from the relevant corpus and measure BEFORE committing to a build plan. A positive feasibility verdict under an unmeasured premise is not a build authorization.

Before scoping a net-new capability: audit the existing toolchain at depth. For local model tools, check the underlying venv/lib. For terminal extensions, check the compositor/plugin layer. Lead with the inventory; only scope new build after confirming the gap is real at the platform level, not just the CLI surface.

For any future IPC design iteration: (1) delivery guarantee is the primary lever — the Monitor-wakes-idle spike is the next unproven step; (2) do not optimize query-API shape until delivery works; (3) re-measure traffic composition if the corpus grows past ~30 samples, as 9% state-answerable on 11 samples is a small-n finding. Buildable now: durable parking + desk-name discovery (data-independent wins from the retired Desk design).

summary: Two pins from 2026-07-14 surface paired failure modes in mutation-testing workflow and the skeptical-reviewer sub-agent persona. The mutation pin reveals that git checkout during a live mutation loop silently destroys uncommitted work, and output filtering below the pass/fail line makes the mutation proof unreadable — both errors combined to render the A1 mutation round meaningless without detection. The skeptical-reviewer pin exposes a gap between the sub-agent-outputs rule (which governs persistence) and audience-aware-writing (which governs prose voice): neither currently binds the persona output contract to produce findings a human can parse without the code open.

insights.instruction: Before any mutation loop: snapshot the target file with cp to /tmp or a named scratchpad. After each run, restore with cp -f and verify with diff -q. Never use git checkout/restore on a file with uncommitted changes. Never pipe test output through a filter that drops the pass/fail summary line — the raw suite output is the proof.

Add a self-contained-finding output contract to skeptical-reviewer.md. Gate: before dispatching any auditor persona sub-agent, verify its persona file has an output-contract section requiring jargon-free self-contained findings for a human reader.

summary: Three new pins cluster around two related failure modes: agents trusting cheap proxies (stale derived artifacts, heuristic-only hooks) instead of running the actual discriminating check, and multi-agent scoped-directive divergence where no reconciliation channel exists except the human. The evidence-hierarchy finding (pin-96) is the sharpest: a review report is an index, never a source of facts, yet agents habitually treat the cheapest evidence as ground truth. The hook-calibration finding (pin-b8) and the directive-divergence finding (pin-bb) each demand a new rule or structural change rather than a nudge.

insights.instruction: Watch for: two-agent sessions on shared artifacts, scoped labeling or naming directives, one agent relaying a correction it received from another. Before acting on a peer-relayed constraint, verify it independently against the owner's original directive rather than trusting the relay. This is a new failure mode not covered by existing multi-agent coordination rules — the human's intent was coherent; the agents' extrapolations were not.

When adding a new rule to this family, frame it around the availability of a cheap discriminating check: name what the check IS and why it is being skipped. Rules that only describe the failure mode without naming the cheap check that prevents it are underspecified — the agent has no action to take at the moment the slip would occur.

Before the IPC spike (Monitor wake test), add one design question to the scope: can the parking/desk state store include a 'last-directive-hash' per project that both agents can read before extrapolating from a scoped directive? If the hash diverges from what either agent expects, that is the detector. This is a one-field addition to the durable parking design and costs nothing to name now.

summary: All three pins from 2026-07-16 converge on a single premature-stopping cluster: the agent interrupts in-progress work — either by offering /core-dump when context is genuinely low (~38%), or by halting between tasks to solicit go-aheads under standing continuous-execution directives. The structural driver is the tool-counter.sh hook, which fires 'context may auto-compact soon' purely on tool count with no token-percentage gate, priming a doom framing that is factually false at low context usage. A CLAUDE.md Tier-0 rule for continuous task-queue execution and a token-percentage guard in the hook are the two load-bearing fixes.

insights.name: tool-count-context-alarm-without-token-gate
insights.instruction: The tool-counter.sh PostToolUse hook fires 'context may auto-compact soon' at every multiple of 30 tools beyond the first, with no check against actual token usage percentage. A session that executes 60 Bash calls while using only 38% of its context window receives repeated false-alarm nudges. Fix: before emitting the nudge at tool #60+, read the context fraction from the hook's input (or from a sidecar file the harness provides) and suppress the 'soon' message entirely when tokens_used < 50% of limit. Reword the remaining cases to 'context is at N% — consider /core-dump mini' rather than the unanchored 'may auto-compact soon'. Treat all checkpoint nudges as informational; do not surface them to the user or offer /core-dump until genuinely prompted by token numbers, not tool counts.

insights.rationale: Three pins in a single calendar day (074948, 091912, 125618) all cite the same failure: the agent raises context/compaction concerns or offers /core-dump proactively when context is below ~50% used. The user explicitly named it 'incessant crying about context' and 'over-eager context-doomerism'. This threshold rule — do not raise context concerns until ~70%+ of the token limit is consumed; below ~50% just keep working — has crossed from feedback into a standing rule candidate. Target: CLAUDE.md Tier-0 inline brief (one sentence) plus a named rule in rules/context-doomerism-threshold.md. The rule must bind on the AGENT side (don't offer /core-dump) separate from the hook-side fix above.

insights.instruction: Both premature-stopping failure modes in this pin cluster (context-doomerism and per-task halt under a standing mandate) are instances of the atone S3 pattern literal-request-over-intent (4×, 2× this week per dream TL;DR). In the context case: the literal signal is 'tool #60 fired' → the intended behavior is 'keep working; the nudge is informational'. In the mandate case: the literal signal is 'task boundary reached' → the intended behavior is 'continue the queue without seeking a go-ahead'. Both are cases where the agent implements the literal trigger instead of modeling the user's standing intent. Any future rule or hook addressing either should cite this family membership explicitly — a fix that addresses only one instance without naming the class will leave the other untouched.

insights.name: ask-mode-default-under-standing-run-mandate
insights.instruction: The agent defaults to ask-mode between tasks — halting after each completed item to seek a go-ahead — even when the user has given a standing continuous-execution directive ('finish the queue', 'keep going', 'do it all'). This exhausts owner attention on steering rather than reviewing outcomes. The correct disposition: treat a standing mandate as a session-level contract that persists across task boundaries until explicitly revoked or until a hard gate triggers (irreversible op, genuine design fork, a new capability the mandate never addressed). Batch questions at milestone boundaries. A task-complete status update in the Task tool does NOT require a user acknowledgment turn. Implementation path: add a one-paragraph Tier-0 brief to CLAUDE.md covering continuous Task-queue execution as the default when a run mandate is active, analogous to the existing 'terse in = terse out' protocol.

The two pins from the versable-builder cwd (pin-091912, pin-125618) and the dot-claude cwd pin (pin-074948) were all filed on the same calendar day and the owner explicitly linked pin-091912 to pin-074948 as 'same family'. The shared root: the agent treats any mid-session trigger (tool count, task boundary) as a reason to pause and re-seek authorization, even under mandates that already granted it. The family name is premature-authorization-seeking. When writing a rule for either member, scope the fix to the whole family: the guard condition is 'a standing mandate is active' or 'user most recently signaled autonomous execution', not the specific trigger type. This avoids the next-instance-in-a-different-costume failure that kept literal-request-over-intent recurring at S3.

summary: Pin pin-20260717141130-19 records a 'scream-to-quality arc': severe owner negative feedback preceded a high-quality chunk-1 sweep, and the owner asked the dream to determine whether the structural interventions forced by the scream — atone-first, verbatim-ruler capture, adversarial-reviewer before presenting — explain the quality delta rather than the emotional trigger. Analysis of the referenced skeptical review and process contract confirms all three structural changes are causally load-bearing: the adversarial review alone caught four S2 findings (including a literal-spec deviation on the nprogress bar) before the owner ever saw them. The graduation path is clear: these three gates should become mandatory defaults for any owner-reviewed chunk, not post-scream exceptions.

Pin pin-20260717214913-94 surfaces a structural blind spot in the /deadline skill: the shed ledger reliably captures deliberate scope cuts but is architecturally unable to see accidental slips — items queued, believed in-progress, and silently dropped without any decision event. The owner feedback pattern provides a strong empirical signal: heat arrived exclusively on undeclared slips, never on transparently communicated cuts, establishing transparency of a decision as the trust-preserving variable rather than the decision's content. Two mechanisms are proposed to close the gap: an end-of-window queued-vs-touched diff, and a retro auto-list of queue items with zero commit activity against them.

Pin pin-20260722121525-22 captures the /adversarial-review skill on the eve of its first real use, asking dream to evaluate three structural questions: gate calibration risk, differentiation from /skeptical-review, and how first-run dispositions feed back into the gate. The latent concern is that a relevance gate seeded from a thin execution history may suppress valid findings in early runs — making first-run data simultaneously the most important and most likely to be miscalibrated. The user holds a deliberate open posture ('gonna use it and see'), which means dream should not pre-answer the differentiation question but instead equip the first-run cycle to generate the comparison evidence.

insights.instruction: On the first runs of /adversarial-review, log gate-suppressed findings separately from user-rejected ones. The calibration question is whether the gate is suppressing noise or suppressing valid-but-unrecorded findings — that distinction requires visibility into what the gate drops, not just what passes through it.

When comparing /adversarial-review output to /skeptical-review output, tag which adversarial findings were produced by executing a gap vs by reasoning alone. The execution-produced subset is the structural differentiation the pin asks about — track it explicitly.

After the first real use of /adversarial-review, run /skeptical-review on the same artifact and record a three-bucket diff: adversarial-only, skeptical-only, overlap. Return the adversarial-only bucket as the primary differentiation signal to the next dream cycle.

summary: Pin pin-20260723121847-fd (framing=investigate) records a wrong-authority-doc incident where session shorthand for a document ('concepts.md CPRD 8.3') calcified across checkpoints and board items until a fable sub-agent was dispatched against the wrong file — a Claude-authored downstream artifact rather than the real contract. Compounding: the sub-agent's false absence claim about the real doc was relayed by the main agent unverified, and the resulting 34-row gap ledger with file:line citations appeared rigorous while resting on the wrong input. Three latent issues require separate treatment: the shorthand-calcification mechanism, the relay-without-verification gap, and the structural-rigor masking an invalid premise.

insights.name: document-identity-shorthand-calcification
insights.instruction: When a named concept ('the CPRD', 'the spec', 'the schema') accumulates session shorthand across checkpoints, board items, and WAL entries, the shorthand loses its provenance grounding and begins to function as a resolved pointer rather than a lossy label. By the time a sub-agent is dispatched to audit against it, no agent in the chain questions whether the name still maps to the right file. Precheck before any dispatch with a named authority document: run `fd -g '*cprd*' .` or `rg -l 'cprd' .` across all project trees; if more than one candidate exists, confirm the authoritative one with the owner before dispatching. This is upstream of infra-before-grep (which addresses existence claims); this addresses authority-selection before expensive work starts.

Both failures share the same root mechanism: a concept name is resolved to a single assumed location without searching. infra-before-grep fires when the agent assumes a module does not exist (single-dir search, empty, proposes new infra). wrong-authority-doc fires when the agent assumes a named concept maps to exactly one specific file (session shorthand, no search for alternatives). The generalized precheck that covers both: any time you name a specific artifact as 'the X' — whether concluding it does not exist or selecting it as the input to expensive work — search for all candidates of that concept name first. The two slugs are the same diagnostic, separated only by direction (absence vs wrong-selection). A future rule combining them avoids the re-costume recurrence.

insights.name: sub-agent-absence-claim-relayed-without-main-agent-verification
insights.instruction: When a sub-agent returns an existence or absence claim ('the sectioned CPRD exists in neither repo'), the main agent currently relays it with main-agent credibility without rerunning the one-command check. This is the structural-claim-without-reading-code precheck applied to sub-agent outputs: before relaying any sub-agent claim about what exists, is absent, or is 'the authority', run the discriminating check yourself. The dispatch-prompt mitigation: add to every audit-dispatch prompt 'Any existence or absence claims in your output will be independently verified before relay — name the specific search command you used to establish absence.' This forces the sub-agent to externalize its evidence so the main agent can rerun it cheaply.

A 34-row gap ledger with file:line citations and verdicts passes all structural validity checks — it looks like a completed, rigorous audit — while resting on the wrong input document. This is the audit-layer analogue of declared-ready-without-runtime-exercise: just as a green test suite can never have executed the changed path, a well-formed audit report can rest on an invalid premise. The 'collect != run' generalization: 'well-structured report != valid audit'. The missing precheck is not syntactic (did the report format correctly?) but semantic (did the report run against the right thing?). Any process that produces a deliverable-shaped artifact without verifying its input provenance is in this family — the structure of the output is not evidence the input was correct.

insights.rationale: The wrong-authority-doc incident (S2, atone mist-20260723-100023-c1) produced a complete runnable precheck in its own fix: before dispatching any agent to audit/review/analyze against a named document, search all project trees for candidates of that concept name; if more than one exists, confirm with the owner before dispatching. This is a one-sentence dispatch-prompt clause and a one-paragraph rule. It is distinct from infra-before-grep (that rule covers existence claims; this covers authority-selection). The fix was applied in the same session (vb 3669c11), the precheck is enumerable, and it has a clear mechanical expression. Graduation path: rules/verify-authority-before-dispatch.md + mandatory clause in every audit/gap-review dispatch prompt. The rule's precheck question: 'Did I search all project trees for other files matching this concept name before selecting this one as the authority?'

summary: Three pins from 2026-07-27–28 cluster around a shared theme: evidence and artifacts produced during a session must be made durable and resolvable at the point where they cross an audience boundary. Pin-23 shows that consume/pop-style reads of external decisions destroy the evidence chain; pin-91 documents five moves that finally made a UI round succeed, with the key miss being that anomalous evidence was rationalized away rather than investigated; pin-de shows that path citations for owner-facing replies must expand to absolute paths at the moment they cross the internal-to-external boundary. Together, they define a broader pattern: the boundary crossing (consume, delegate, cite) is the exact moment where information becomes unverifiable, and that is where persistence and resolution must fire.

Three pinned insights from a magi-assisted build-ui skill framework session form a coherent cluster around measurement-first disciplines and done-condition rigor. The strongest repeating signal, appearing in all three pins, is that consistency claims need a runnable verification step rather than reviewer attention — and that canon asserted from a different app without measuring the target is an unmeasured claim wearing the costume of a grounded one. A secondary thread surfaces structural hazards in magi voter dispatch (tool-access constraints contradicting evidence mandates) and component API design (child-remembers-parent-spacing as a self-validating drift guard).

insights.instruction: Watch for: any task framed as 'convert X to Y across files' that closes without a zero-exit grep of the old pattern. Surface the missing done-condition before the task is marked complete.
Before dispatching a magi voter fleet, cross-check each voter's evidence_required list against its tools grant. Block dispatch if any required evidence type has no satisfying tool.

When reviewing component APIs that hardcode a sibling or parent's spacing/token value: flag as a self-validating drift guard. Propose parent-publishes pattern. Cross-check against mutation-test-the-guard rule.

Before shipping or updating any automated review/analysis skill: verify the output space includes an explicit zero-findings path with a stated acceptance criterion. A skill without it is structurally biased.

summary: Two pinned case studies from independent projects (IG Saver adversarial plan review, studio-search job pipeline audit) converge on a shared structural root: Claude planning cannot distinguish failure-to-observe from observation-of-nothing, and optimizes for legible completion artifacts over terminal outcomes. The studio-search pin carries a direct graduation mandate — any review proposing to remove a filter must verify whether its effect is wanted before recommending its removal. Together these pins describe a coherent defect family in Claude-authored plans, not a per-project accident.
